s: At the founding of the All India Kisan Sabha in April 1936 at Lucknow, who were its President and Secretary respectively?
o: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati and N.G. Ranga
N.G. Ranga and Swami Sahajanand Saraswati
Swami Sahajanand Saraswati and Kommareddi Satyanarayana
x: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati (who had founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929) was President and N.G. Ranga was Secretary. Option B reverses the two; Nehru and Baba Ramchandra set up the Oudh Kisan Sabha (1920); Kommareddi Satyanarayana led the 1937 Rythu Yatra.

s: Which body did N.G. Ranga found in 1943 after leaving the All India Kisan Sabha?
x: When the communist-led AIKS backed the People's War line, Ranga left and founded the Andhra Rashtra Kisan Congress in 1943.

s: The All India Kisan Sabha worked as the peasant wing of which party?
x: The AIKS worked as the peasant wing of the Congress and demanded abolition of zamindari and cancellation of debts.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the All India Kisan Sabha?
o: It was first named the All India Kisan Congress
It was founded at Palasa in 1940
x: AIKS was founded in April 1936 at Lucknow; Palasa hosted a session in March 1940.

s: When was the Palasa session of the All India Kisan Sabha, presided over by Sahajanand, held?
x: The Palasa AIKS session was in March 1940; Ranga was jailed for defying his confinement.

s: What did the All India United Kisan Sabha, formed by Sahajanand Saraswati before his death in 1950, demand?
x: The All India United Kisan Sabha demanded nationalisation of land and waterways.

s: In which year was the All India Kisan Sabha, first named the All India Kisan Congress, founded?
x: The All India Kisan Sabha was founded in April 1936 at Lucknow; 1940 was its Palasa session.

s: Which demand did N.G. Ranga's memorandum to the Whitley Commission in 1929 mainly reflect?
x: N. G. Ranga’s 1929 memorandum to the Whitley Commission raised the demand for minimum wages.

s: Besides MSP and minimum wages, which of the following was a demand of the Kisan movement in Andhra?
x: The Kisan movement demanded MSP, minimum wages and zamindari abolition.

s: Which award did N.G. Ranga receive in 1991?
x: Ranga, called Rythu Bandhu and Acharya, received the Padma Vibhushan in 1991, not the Bharat Ratna.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding N.G. Ranga is correct?
o: He founded the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham alone in 1915.
He was known as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement.
He led the 1937 Rythu Yatra as a village association organiser.
x: N.G. Ranga was known as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement. The Munagala Award was authored by Gottipati Brahmaiah, while the 1937 Rythu Yatra was led by Kommareddi Satyanarayana.

s: Who is called the 'Father of the Indian Peasant Movement'?
x: N.G. Ranga is known as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement and Rythu Bandhu.

s: What was the original name of Acharya N.G. Ranga?
x: N.G. Ranga's full name was Gogineni Ranganayakulu.

s: Which of the following is NOT a book associated with N.G. Ranga?
x: Credo of World Peasantry, Revolutionary Peasantry and Fight for Freedom are books associated with N.G. Ranga. The Munagala Award was authored by Gottipati Brahmaiah and is not a book of Ranga.

s: Which one of the following journals is correctly matched with its place or founder?
x: Prajavani was the Vizag journal. Praja Bandhu and Navayuga were N.G. Ranga's journals, not Nellore's, and Zamin Ryot came from Nellore, not Vizag.

s: In which year did N.G. Ranga found the Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu?
x: The Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu dates from 1939; the Nidubrolu school from 1933-34.

s: Where was the Indian Peasants Institute founded by N.G. Ranga located?
x: The Indian Peasants Institute (first Kisan School) was at Nidubrolu, Guntur, in 1933-34.

s: Which of the following were journals of N.G. Ranga?
o: Credo of World Peasantry and Fight for Freedom
x: Praja Bandhu and Navayuga were Ranga's journals; Credo of World Peasantry and Fight for Freedom are his books.

s: Who among the following authored the Munagala Award?
x: Gottipati Brahmaiah authored the Munagala Award. He was also a pioneer of the zamindari ryot movement and Secretary of the APCC.

s:
Consider the following persons:
1. Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao
2. Gouthu Latchanna
3. Gottipati Brahmaiah
Who among the above were Srikakulam kisan leaders?
x: Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao and Gouthu Latchanna were Srikakulam kisan leaders; Gottipati Brahmaiah is linked with the zamindari ryot movement and the Munagala Award.

s: Which Andhra kisan leader was called 'Rythu Pedda'?
x: Gottipati Brahmaiah was called 'Rythu Pedda'; Ranga was 'Rythu Bandhu'.

s: Which Andhra kisan leader later served as Chairman of the AP Legislative Council (1964-68)?
x: Gottipati Brahmaiah, 'Rythu Pedda', was Chairman of the AP Legislative Council (1964-68) and got the Padma Bhushan (1982).

s: Which Srikakulam kisan leader died in jail after the Mandasa protest?
x: Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao died in jail after the Mandasa protest.

s: Who led the 1931 Divi Taluk Resettlement Mahasabha movement?
x: Gottipati Brahmaiah led the 1931 Divi Taluk movement; Ranga led the 1935 Guntur anti-resettlement movement.

s: Who led the 1933 Ryot agitation of Andhra?
x: N.G. Ranga led the historic Ryot Agitation of Andhra in 1933 (APPSC FRO key); Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary led the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign of 1921-22.

s: Who led the Guntur anti-resettlement movement of 1935?
x: N.G. Ranga led the 1935 Guntur anti-resettlement movement.

s: Where was the 1931 no-tax resolution of the Divi taluk Resettlement Mahasabha passed?
x: The Divi taluk Resettlement Mahasabha met at Mopidevi in 1931 under Gottipati Brahmaiah.

s: In which year was the Krishna District Rythu Sangham, an early peasant body in Andhra, formed?
x: The Krishna District Rythu Sangham was formed in 1915; Guntur and Godavari sanghams came in 1923.

s: In which year was the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham founded?
x: The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was founded in 1928. It merged into the AIKS in 1936.

s: Who was the first General Secretary of the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham?
x: B.V. Ratnam was the first General Secretary; Ranga, Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana and Maganti Bapineedu were its founders.

s: Which of the following was NOT a founder of the Andhra Provincial Ryots Association (1928)?
x: Ranga, Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana and Maganti Bapineedu founded it; B.V. Ratnam was its first General Secretary.

s: In which year did the Andhra Provincial Ryots Association merge into the All India Kisan Sabha?
x: It merged into AIKS in 1936.

s: To which Speaker was a memorandum submitted at the end of the Ichchapuram-Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra (1937)?
x: The memorandum went to Speaker Bulusu Sambamurthy; Prakasam was then Revenue Minister.

s: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was compared to which national movement?
x: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was compared to the Dandi March. It ended with a memorandum submitted to Speaker Bulusu Sambamurthy.

s: On which date did N.G. Ranga launch the Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra?
x: Ranga launched the yatra on 3 July 1937.

s: Who led the 1937 Rythu Rakshana Yatra on the ground?
x: Ranga launched the yatra, but Kommareddi Satyanarayana led it on the ground.

s: Munagala paragana was situated in which administrative area at the time of the struggle?
x: Munagala paragana was located in Nandigama taluk of Krishna district at the time. It is now associated with Suryapet/Nalgonda.

s: Who was the zamindar of Munagala?
x: Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao was the zamindar of Munagala. Though a literary patron, he was described as a harsh landlord.

s: Who led the Kalukova Satyagraha of 1938 over the paddy wage?
x: The 1938 Kalukova Satyagraha was led by Nanduri Prasada Rao over the 80-seers-per-acre wage; the Sub-Collector made the zamindar pay.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Munagala paragana struggle:
1. Munagala was then in Nandigama taluk of Krishna district.
2. The agitation was withdrawn on 19 June 1939 after Prakasam and Ranga promised action.
3. The Brahmaiah Award covered 124 villages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Munagala was in Nandigama taluk, Krishna, and the agitation was withdrawn on 19 June 1939; the Brahmaiah Award covered 142 villages, not 124.

s: The Brahmaiah Award of 15 January 1939 in the Munagala struggle covered how many villages?
x: The Brahmaiah Award (15 Jan 1939) was a settlement covering 142 villages.

s: On which date was 'Munagala Day' observed?
x: Munagala Day was 11 June 1939; the agitation was withdrawn on 19 June 1939.

s: Munagala paragana, once in Krishna district, is now part of which district?
x: Munagala was in Nandigama taluk, Krishna district, and is now in Suryapet/Nalgonda.

s: In which year did the firing over Kishkindapalem land, which killed four persons in the Challapalli struggle, take place?
x: The Kishkindapalem firing was in 1946, after the temple land grab (1939) and Rajeswara Rao and Chapanayya's leadership (1942), and before the July 1947 land occupation.

s: Who led the June 1930 revolt of Potharlanka, Ghantasala and Movva farmers in the Challapalli struggle?
x: Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya led the June 1930 revolt; Rajeswara Rao and Chapanayya led in 1942.

s: In 1939, the Challapalli zamindar grabbed how many acres of temple land?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (6,000); it is added as option 5.
NextGen gives the Challapalli zamindar's grab of Andhra Mahavishnu temple land as 6,000 acres; the old app notes' '600' looks like a dropped zero.

s: Up to which year did the Union Cabinet extend PM-KISAN in August 2026?
x: PM-KISAN was extended to 2030-31 with an outlay of Rs 3.15 lakh crore.

s: Who led the Challapalli zamindari struggle in 1942?
o: Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya
Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya and Nanduri Prasada Rao
Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao
x: In 1942 the Challapalli struggle was led by Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya, who were both jailed.

s: In which year did farmers occupy the surplus land of the Challapalli zamindar?
x: In July 1947 the farmers occupied the zamindar's surplus land, ending the Challapalli struggle.

s: Who led the Kisan (agrarian) movement in Andhra?
x: N.G. Ranga led the Kisan movement; Veerayya Chowdary led the No-Tax Campaign and Kanneganti Hanumanthu the Palnadu forest satyagraha.

s: Who led the Khond rising?
x: The Khond rising was led by Chakra Bisoi; Budhu Bhagat led the Kol rising and Sidhu and Kanhu the Santhal Hul.

s: The Tamar tribal rising is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Oraon tribes and Tamar in Jharkhand
Bhil tribes and Khandesh in Maharashtra
x: The Tamar rising was associated with the Oraon tribes and the Tamar region of present-day Jharkhand. Its recorded period was 1789–1832.

s: In which year did the Ahom rebellion begin?
x: The Ahom rebellion began in 1828, before the Kol rising (1831-32), the Santhal Hul (1855-56) and the Ulgulan (1899-1900).

s: Who led the Khasi rising of 1829–33?
x: The Khasi rising of 1829–33 was associated with Tirot Sing. Gomadhar Konwar led the Ahom rebellion.

s: To whom did the Company hand over Upper Assam after the Ahom rebellion?
x: The Ahom rebellion forced the East India Company to hand Upper Assam to Purandar Singh.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Tana Bhagat movement (1914, Chotanagpur) was led by Jatra Bhagat, an Oraon. The Kol rising was led by Budhu Bhagat; Birsa (born 1875) led the 1899-1900 Ulgulan, so linking him to the Kol rising is a known error. Gomadhar Konwar led the Ahom rebellion; the Khasi rising was under Tirot Sing. The Bhumij rising was led by Ganga Narayan.

s: Which rebellion did Bakshi Jagabandhu lead?
x: Bakshi Jagabandhu led the Paika Rebellion in Odisha (1817).

s: Where did the Bhil rising of 1818-31 take place?
x: The Bhil rising of 1818-31 was in Khandesh (Maharashtra); Singhbhum, Ghumsar and Barabhum were the regions of the Ho, Khond and Bhumij risings.

s: Ganga Narain is associated with which tribal revolt?
x: Ganga Narain led the Bhumij revolt of 1832-33 in Barabhum, Manbhum; the Kol rising was led by Budhu Bhagat.

s: Who led the Ho revolt of 1820-21 in Singhbhum?
x: The Ho revolt in Singhbhum was led by the Raja of Parahat.

s: In which region did the Khond rising led by Chakra Bisoi take place?
x: The Khond rising (1837-56) under Chakra Bisoi was in Ghumsar, Odisha hills.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Indigo Revolt was in 1859–60; the Sanyasi-Fakir Rebellion was in the 18th century, the Paika Rebellion in 1817 and the Deccan Riots in 1875.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Paika Rebellion took place in 1817.
The Santhal Rebellion took place in 1859–60.
The Indigo Revolt took place in 1859–60.
The Kol Rebellion took place in 1831–32.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Santhal Rebellion was in 1855–56, while 1859–60 is the Indigo Revolt. The other dates are correct.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Paika Rebellion occurred in Odisha.
The Indigo Revolt occurred in Maharashtra.
The Deccan Riots occurred in Maharashtra.
The Santhal Rebellion occurred in the Bengal/Bihar region.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Indigo Revolt of 1859–60 took place in Bengal. The Deccan Riots were in Maharashtra, and the other statements are right.

s: When did the Kol Rebellion take place?
x: The Kol Rebellion was in 1831-32; Paika 1817, Santhal 1855-56 and Pabna 1873-76.

s: Where did the Sanyasi-Fakir Rebellion take place?
x: The Sanyasi-Fakir Rebellion was in Bengal, the Paika Rebellion in Odisha, the Deccan Riots in Maharashtra and the Rampa Rebellion in Andhra.

s: Which of the following took place last?
x: The Rampa Rebellion of 1922–24 came after the Indigo Revolt (1859–60), the Deccan Riots (1875) and the Munda Ulgulan (1899–1900).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Pabna Agrarian Movement was associated with peasants.
2. The Deccan Riots were associated with indigo cultivators.
3. The Rampa Rebellion was associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Deccan Riots were by peasants against moneylenders; indigo cultivators belong to the Indigo Revolt.

s: Who led the Jaintia rising of 1860-62?
x: U Kiang Nangbah led the Jaintia rising against house tax and income tax; Tirot Sing led the Khasi rising of 1829-33.

s: Where was U Kiang Nangbah, leader of the Jaintia rising, hanged in December 1862?
x: U Kiang Nangbah was hanged at Jowai on 30 December 1862.

s: What triggered the Kuki rising of 1917-19 in Manipur?
o: Forced recruitment into the Labour Corps for France
The imposition of house tax and income tax
x: The Kuki rising was set off by forced recruitment into the Labour Corps for France during the First World War.

s:
Arrange the following tribal revolts in chronological order:
1. Khasi rising
2. Paika Bidroha
3. Jaintia rising
4. Santhal Hul
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Paika Bidroha (1817), Khasi rising (1829-33), Santhal Hul (1855-56) and Jaintia rising (1860-62) is the correct order.

s: Against which taxes was the Jaintia rising of 1860-62 mainly directed?
x: The Jaintia rising under U Kiang Nangbah was against house tax and income tax.

s: In which present-day state did the Paika Bidroha of 1817 take place?
x: The Paika Bidroha under Bakshi Jagabandhu broke out at Khurda in Odisha, not West Bengal.

s: Oppression by whom was an important cause of the Santhal Hul?
x: The Santhals rose against oppression by zamindars, moneylenders (the dikus) and the police.

s: Which of the following groups was associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul in addition to Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu?
o: Chand, Bhairav and the sisters Phulo-Jhano
Jatra Bhagat, Govind Giri and Motilal Tejawat
Umaji Naik, Chittur Singh and Narayan Rao
Ganga Narayan, Budhu Bhagat and Tirot Sing
x: Chand and Bhairav, along with the sisters Phulo and Jhano, were associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul.

s: Hul Divas is observed on which date?
x: Hul Divas is observed on 30 June.

s: What was the tract demarcated for Santhal settlement in the Rajmahal Hills called?
x: After failing to control the Paharias, the British settled the Santhals in the tract called Damin-i-Koh.

s: What did the British do after the Santhal Hul?
o: enacted the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act in 1876
made Santhal Parganas a separate district with laws protecting tribal land
placed Kolhan under the Munda-Manki system
transferred the Santhal areas to Assam
x: After the Hul, Santhal Parganas was created as a separate district with special laws to protect tribal land; the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act came later, in 1908.

s: Where did the Santhal Hul of 1855 begin?
x: The Hul began at Bhognadih on 30 June 1855, observed as Hul Divas.

s: Approximately how many Santhals were killed when the Hul was crushed in 1856?
x: Over 15,000 Santhals were killed; about 30,000 had proclaimed Santhal Raj.

s: After the Santhal Hul, the Santhal Parganas was made into which of the following?
x: Santhal Parganas became a separate non-regulation district (Act XXXVII of 1855) with laws protecting tribal land.

s: Which hill people did the British fail to control in the Rajmahal Hills before inviting the Santhals to settle there?
x: The British could not control the Paharias of the Rajmahal Hills, so they invited the Santhals to settle in the Damin-i-Koh.

s: The destruction of which system was the immediate agrarian grievance behind Birsa Munda's revolt?
x: The revolt was caused in part by the destruction of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system by zamindars, thikadars and missionaries.

s: Birsa Munda, revered as 'Dharti Aba', led the Ulgulan in a region that is today part of which state?
x: Birsa Munda (Dharti Aba, 'Father of the Earth') led the Ulgulan of 1899-1900 in Chotanagpur, present-day Jharkhand (APPSC 2024). Odisha was the scene of the Paika Bidroha, Maharashtra of the Ramosi and Bhil risings, and Andhra of the Rampa rebellions.

s: On which date is Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, the birth anniversary of Birsa Munda, observed?
x: Janjatiya Gaurav Divas is 15 November; 30 June is Hul Divas of the Santhals.

s: What was Birsa Munda's religious movement, which blended Munda tradition with Hinduism and Christianity, called?
x: Birsa Munda founded the monotheist Birsait faith, which blended elements of Munda tradition, Hinduism and Christianity.

s: Which one of the following was NOT part of Birsa Munda’s social and religious reform programme?
o: Opposition to animal sacrifice and spirit worship
Promotion of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system
x: Birsa’s programme opposed liquor, witchcraft, animal sacrifice and spirit worship and promoted a monotheist faith. Khuntkatti was a landholding system whose destruction helped cause the revolt; it was not a religious reform practice.

s: What did 'Abua Raj', the aim of the Munda Ulgulan (1899-1900), mean?
x: The Ulgulan of 1899-1900, involving about 6,000 Mundas, aimed at Abua Raj or self-rule.

s: What did the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908 do?
o: barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and recognised Khuntkatti rights
introduced the Permanent Settlement in Chotanagpur
x: The 1908 Act, a consequence of the Ulgulan, barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and recognised Khuntkatti rights.

s: Where did Birsa Munda die on 9 June 1900?
x: Birsa Munda died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900.

s: Where was Birsa Munda captured on 3 February 1900?
x: Birsa was captured in the Jamkopai forest near Chakradharpur (West Singhbhum) on 3 February 1900.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correct about Birsa Munda?
o: He led the Kol rising of 1831-32
x: The Kol rising of 1831-32 was led by Budhu Bhagat; Birsa was born only in 1875.

s: Where is the Bhagwan Birsa Munda Memorial Udyan cum Freedom Fighters Museum (2021) located?
x: The museum was opened at Ranchi in 2021.

s:
Consider the following statements about tribal land laws:
1. The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908 recognised Khuntkatti rights.
2. The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act was passed before the Ulgulan of 1899-1900.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The CNT Act of 1908 recognised Khuntkatti rights, but it came after Birsa's Ulgulan of 1899-1900.

s: What was the Rampa Rebellion of 1879–80 mainly directed against?
o: the imprisonment of Jamedar Chida Khan
the disbanding of the Vizianagaram troops
the Permanent Settlement imposed on Narayana Babu
Munsubar Madhava Bhupati Dev and oppressive taxation
x: The 1879–80 Rampa Rebellion in the Rampachodavaram Agency opposed Munsubar Madhava Bhupati Dev and oppressive taxes. Madhava Bhupati Dev had been appointed in 1848.

s: The Rekapalle revolt of 1879 followed a rise in the podu tax from 4 annas to how much per axe?
x: The podu tax was raised from 4 annas to 4-12 annas per axe during a famine.

s: Who led the Gond movement of 1938-44 in Hyderabad State?
x: Komaram Bheem led the Gond movement (1938-44) in Hyderabad State.

s: Which of the following rebellions took place in the Andhra region?
x: The Rampa Rebellion took place in the Andhra region; the other three are linked with Bengal.

s: During the Rekapalle rising of 1879, Ambul Reddy raided which police station?
x: Ambul Reddy raided Vaddagudem police station on 10 July 1879; the rising was triggered by a rise in the podu tax during a famine.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Rampa rebellions:
1. The 1879–80 rebellion was led by local Agency leaders such as Chandrayya and Ambul Reddy.
2. The 1922–24 rebellion was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: The 1879–80 rebellion was led by local figures including Chandrayya, Tammanna Dora, Pulikantha Sambaiah and Ambul Reddy; Alluri Sitarama Raju led the later 1922–24 rebellion.

s: When did the Gulugonda revolt take place?
x: The Gulugonda revolt was in 1845-48; Rampa-Rekapalle 1879, Alluri's Rampa Rebellion 1922-24 and Komaram Bheem's Gond movement 1938-44.

s: The Gulugonda revolt of 1845–48 was associated with which of the following persons?
x: The Gulugonda revolt in the Vizag region during 1845–48 was associated with Chinna Bhupathi.

s: During the Rampa rising of 1879, Darabandala Chandrayya burnt which police station?
x: Chandrayya burnt the Addatheegala police station; Ambul Reddy attacked Vaddagudem.

s: Who led the Koya rising of 1879-80?
x: Tomas (Tomma) Dora led the Koya rising of 1879-80.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Komaram Bheem's Gond movement was of 1938-44; the other pairs are correct.

s: Against which law was the Rampa Rebellion of 1922-24 under Alluri Sitarama Raju mainly directed?
x: Alluri Sitarama Raju's Rampa Rebellion of 1922-24 rose against the Madras Forest Act of 1882, which curbed tribal forest rights.

s: Against which laws was the Rekapalle revolt of 1879 in Bhadrachalam taluk mainly directed?
x: The Rekapalle rising of 1879 was against forest laws and higher podu tax that hurt the hill tribes.

s: In which area did the Rampa rebellion of 1879-80 break out?
x: The Rampa rebellion of 1879-80 broke out in the Rampachodavaram Agency of Godavari district against the mansabdar and taxes.

s: During which years did Komaram Bheem lead the Gond movement?
x: Komaram Bheem's Gond movement was in 1938-44.

s: Which tribes took part in Alluri Sitarama Raju's Rampa Rebellion of 1922-24?
x: Alluri's Rampa Rebellion was a rising of the Koyas and Konda Doras.

s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the Ramosi uprisings in Maharashtra?
x: Chittur Singh, Umaji Naik and Bapu Trimbakji Sawant led the Ramosis, who rose after the fall of the Peshwa. Narayan Rao is not linked to the Ramosis (APPSC 2019 trap).

s: Which event did the Ramosi risings in Maharashtra follow?
x: The Ramosis rose after the fall of the Peshwa, in 1822 and again in 1825-26 around Satara.

s: Against what did Govind Giri, also known as Guru, mainly lead the Bhils?
x: Govind Giri led the Bhils against bonded labour. His movement was associated with Rajasthan and Gujarat.

s: In which year was Mangarh Dham declared a National Monument?
x: Mangarh Dham, associated with the 1913 massacre, became a National Monument in 2022.

s: Who led the Eki movement (1921-22) in Mewar?
x: Motilal Tejawat led the Eki movement in Mewar; Govind Giri led the Lasodia movement.

s: In which year did Govind Giri found the Samp Sabha among the Bhils?
x: Govind Giri founded the Samp Sabha in 1883; 1913 is the year of the Mangarh massacre.

s: In which year did the Mangarh massacre of Bhils, called the 'Adivasi Jallianwala', take place?
x: The Mangarh massacre was in 1913; Mangarh Dham became a National Monument in 2022.

s: By what name is the Mangarh massacre of 1913 popularly known?
x: The Mangarh massacre of 1913 is called the “Adivasi Jallianwala.” Mangarh Dham was later recognised as a National Monument.

s: How did the Indian Forest Act of 1878, which added to tribal discontent, treat forests?
x: The 1878 Act made forests state property, strengthening state control and hurting tribal customary rights.

s: In the context of tribal revolts, whom did the term 'dikus' mainly refer to?
x: Dikus were outsiders such as moneylenders, zamindars and traders whose activities contributed to tribal land alienation.

s: The Paikas lost their rent-free lands after the British conquest of Odisha in which year?
x: The Paikas lost rent-free lands after the 1803 conquest and resented salt policy and revenue burdens.

s: Through whom did Wilkinson's Rule (1837) govern the Kolhan?
x: After the Kol rising, Wilkinson's Rule of 1837 governed the Kolhan through the Munda-Manki chiefs.

s: Of which district was Cleveland the Collector when he framed his conciliatory plan for the Paharias in the 1780s?
x: Cleveland, Collector of Bhagalpur in the 1780s, ruled the Paharias through their hill chiefs.

s: In which year was the Santhal Parganas Tenancy (Supplementary Provisions) Act passed?
x: The SPT Act is of 1949; 1908 is the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act and 1872 the Santhal Parganas Settlement Regulation.

s: In tribal history, what does 'Khuntkatti' refer to?
o: A reform item of Birsa Munda
x: Khuntkatti was the joint landholding system of the Mundas, not a reform of Birsa; its destruction led to the Ulgulan.

s: What does the term 'Meriah' refer to?
x: Meriah was the human sacrifice of the Khonds; its ban helped cause the Khond rising.

s: What does the term 'Podu' refer to?
x: Podu means shifting cultivation; curbs on it caused tribal risings.

s: Who were the President and the General Secretary respectively of the Congress Socialist Party at its founding in 1934?
o: Jayaprakash Narayan and Acharya Narendra Dev
Acharya Narendra Dev and Jayaprakash Narayan
Ram Manohar Lohia and Asoka Mehta
Acharya Narendra Dev and Ram Manohar Lohia
x: Acharya Narendra Dev was President and Jayaprakash Narayan General Secretary of the CSP (1934); Ram Manohar Lohia was among the founders but not General Secretary. Option A reverses the two posts, option D wrongly makes Lohia General Secretary, and option C pairs Lohia with Asoka Mehta (linked with the Hind Mazdoor Sabha, 1948).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Congress Socialist Party:
1. It was founded at Patna in May 1934.
2. Its policies were fixed at Bombay in October 1934.
3. Jawaharlal Nehru formally joined it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The CSP was founded at Patna in May 1934 and its policies were fixed at Bombay in October 1934; Nehru did not formally join it.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correct about the Congress Socialist Party?
o: Ram Manohar Lohia was its first General Secretary
Acharya Narendra Dev was its President
It was founded at Patna in 1934
Jayaprakash Narayan was its General Secretary
x: Lohia was a founder; Jayaprakash Narayan was the General Secretary.

s: Under whom was India's first May Day organised at Madras in 1923?
x: The Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan under M. Singaravelu Chettiar held India's first May Day at Madras in 1923.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Madras Labour Union — S.A. Dange and communists
Girni Kamgar Union — S.A. Dange and communists
Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association — Gandhi with Anasuya Sarabhai
x: The Madras Labour Union was founded by B.P. Wadia. S.A. Dange and communists were associated with the Girni Kamgar Union.

s: Who founded the Girni Kamgar Union of Bombay (1928)?
x: The Girni Kamgar Union was founded in 1928 by S.A. Dange and the communists; B.P. Wadia founded the Madras Labour Union.

s: Along with whom did Gandhi found the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association (1920)?
x: Gandhi founded the Majoor Mahajan Sangh with Anasuya Sarabhai, its president for life.

s: The Madras Labour Union (1918), the first trade union in India, was formed among the workers of which mills?
x: B.P. Wadia formed the Madras Labour Union among workers of the Buckingham and Carnatic Mills.

s: By what other name is the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association known?
x: The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association (1920) is also called the Majoor Mahajan Sangh; Anasuya Sarabhai was its president for life.

s: Which founding of the CPI does the CPI itself recognise?
x: The CPI recognises Kanpur, 26 December 1925; the CPI(M) recognises Tashkent, 1920.

s: In which year was the British ban imposed on the Communist Party of India in 1934 lifted?
x: The ban of 23 July 1934 was lifted in 1942; Hyderabad State banned the CPI in 1946.

s: On which date was the Communist Party of India formally founded in India at the Kanpur conference?
x: The CPI was formally founded in India at Kanpur on 26 December 1925.

s: In 1964, the Communist Party of India split into the CPI and which other party?
x: The CPI split in 1964 into the CPI and the Communist Party of India (Marxist), or CPI(M).

s: At the Ahmedabad Congress of 1921, who moved the demand for complete independence along with Hasrat Mohani?
x: Hasrat Mohani and Swami Kumarananda moved it at Ahmedabad; Roy and Abani Mukherji are linked with the Tashkent founding of the CPI.

s: From which month and year did the Communist Party support the “People's War” line?
x: The Communist Party backed the “People's War” line from June 1941.

s: The Communist Party of India was banned in Hyderabad State in:
x: The CPI was banned in Hyderabad State in 1946; the British all-India ban of 1934 was lifted in 1942.

s: From which place and year does the Communist Party of India (Marxist) date its founding?
x: The CPI(M) dates the party from Tashkent 1920, while the CPI dates itself from the Kanpur conference of 1925.

s: Where was the Communist Party of India set up in October 1920 by M.N. Roy and others?
x: M.N. Roy and others set up the Communist Party of India at Tashkent on 17 October 1920, after the 2nd Comintern Congress.

s: Who among the following was NOT among the founders of the Communist Party of India at Tashkent in 1920?
x: M.N. Roy, Abani Mukherjee and M.P.T. Acharya founded the CPI at Tashkent; S.A. Dange was a leader in India.

s: Who organised the Kanpur conference of December 1925, where the Communist Party of India was formally founded?
x: Satyabhakta organised the Kanpur conference of 26 December 1925.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Communist Party of India was formally founded in India at Kanpur in December 1925.
2. The Kanpur conference was organised by M.N. Roy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The CPI was formally founded at Kanpur on 26 December 1925; the conference was organised by Satyabhakta, not M.N. Roy.

s: Who founded the RSS at Nagpur in 1925, the same year as the CPI's Kanpur conference?
x: The RSS was founded by K.B. Hedgewar at Nagpur on 27 September 1925.

s: Who was the General Secretary of the All India Trade Union Congress at the time of its formation?
x: Diwan Chaman Lal was the General Secretary of the AITUC at its formation.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: INTUC — established by the Congress in 1947
RTUC — established in 1947 by the Congress
National Trades Union Federation — first May Day organisation
x: The Congress set up the Indian National Trade Union Congress in 1947. The AITUC moderates broke away in 1929, leading to RTUC and later the National Trades Union Federation.

s: Who was the Vice President of AITUC at its founding in 1920?
x: Joseph Baptista was Vice President; Lajpat Rai presided and Diwan Chaman Lal was General Secretary.

s: In which year did the Congress set up the Indian National Trade Union Congress (INTUC)?
x: INTUC was set up in 1947; AITUC dates from 1920 and the Hind Mazdoor Sabha from 1948.

s: Who presided over the first session of the All India Trade Union Congress held at Bombay in 1920?
x: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the first AITUC session at Bombay in 1920; Joseph Baptista was Vice President and Diwan Chaman Lal General Secretary.

s: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the first session of which organisation in 1920?
x: The All India Trade Union Congress was founded at Bombay on 31 October 1920 with Lala Lajpat Rai as the president of its first session.

s: In which city was the All India Trade Union Congress founded on 31 October 1920?
x: AITUC was founded at Bombay on 31 October 1920.

s: Who among the following was a co-founder of the AITUC and later became its General Secretary?
x: N.M. Joshi was a co-founder of the AITUC and later its General Secretary; B.P. Wadia founded the Madras Labour Union.

s:
Arrange the following trade union bodies in the order of their founding:
1. INTUC
2. CITU
3. AITUC
4. Hind Mazdoor Sabha
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: AITUC (1920), INTUC (1947), Hind Mazdoor Sabha (1948) and CITU (1970) is the correct order.

s: After the 1929 split in the AITUC, the moderates formed which body?
o: RTUC, later the National Trades Union Federation
Indian Trade Union Federation (later the National Trades Union Federation)
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Indian Trade Union Federation (later the National Trades Union Federation)); it is added as option 5.
After the 1929 Nagpur split the moderates under N.M. Joshi formed the Indian Trade Union Federation (V.V. Giri president), later merged into the National Trades Union Federation. The Red Trade Union Congress (RTUC) was the communists' breakaway of 1931, INTUC came in 1947 and HMS in 1948.

s: In which year was the first Factories Act, which curbed child labour, passed?
x: The first Factories Act came in 1881, after the Bombay factory commission of 1875; the Act of 1891 followed.

s: Whose March 1921 resolution led to the Trade Unions Act, 1926?
x: The Act, giving registered unions legal status and protection from conspiracy suits, followed N.M. Joshi's March 1921 resolution.

s: Who called the Trade Disputes Act, 1929 the 'Slavery of India Bill'?
x: Motilal Nehru called it the 'Slavery of India Bill'; it banned sympathetic strikes and imposed long notice periods.

s: In which year did the Royal Commission on Labour (Whitley Commission), appointed in 1929, submit its report?
x: The Whitley Commission was appointed in 1929 and reported in 1931.

s: What was the Public Safety Bill of 1929 aimed at?
o: Foreign communists such as Philip Spratt
x: The Public Safety Bill targeted foreign communists like Philip Spratt; the Trade Disputes Act banned sympathetic strikes.

s: The year 2026 marks the completion of how many years of the Trade Unions Act, 1926?
x: The year 2026 marks 100 years of the Trade Unions Act, 1926.

s: What did the Trade Unions Act, 1926 provide for?
o: Registration and legal status for trade unions
A system of tribunals and a ban on sympathetic strikes
A weekly holiday for factory workers
Limits on child labour in factories
x: The Trade Unions Act, 1926 gave trade unions registration and legal status; tribunals came with the Trade Disputes Act, 1929.

s: Which Factories Act provided a weekly holiday and limited the working hours of women?
x: The Factories Act of 1891 gave a weekly holiday and limited women's working hours.

s: How many labour and communist leaders were tried in the Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929)?
x: 31 leaders, including Dange, Muzaffar Ahmad, Usmani and Philip Spratt, were tried; the long trial made them martyrs.

s: Against whom were the Peshawar conspiracy cases (1922-27) directed?
o: Leaders of the Girni Kamgar Union
Members of the Congress Socialist Party
Organisers of the Workers and Peasants Party
Muhajirs trained in Moscow and Tashkent
x: The Peshawar cases tried Muhajirs who had trained in Moscow and Tashkent and were arrested on return across the North-West Frontier.

s: Which British communist was among the accused in the Meerut Conspiracy Case of 1929?
x: Philip Spratt was tried in the Meerut case along with Dange, Muzaffar Ahmad and Usmani.

s: Which organisation sought to make the Congress more revolutionary and to organise the common people?
x: The Workers and Peasants Party sought a more radical Congress; the Radhasoami Satsang stressed one God, the Guru, Satsang and spiritual life.

s: Under what name did the Workers and Peasants Party begin at Calcutta in 1925?
x: It began as the Labour Swaraj Party (Kazi Nazrul Islam, Hemanta Kumar Sarkar) and was renamed the Workers and Peasants Party of Bengal in 1926.

s: Who founded the Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan in 1923?
x: M. Singaravelu founded the Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan in 1923.

s: With whom were the journals Navayug and Langal associated?
x: Muzaffar Ahmad was associated with the journals Navayug and Langal.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Vanguard was edited by M.N. Roy and was the first communist paper. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: Who edited the journal 'The Socialist'?
x: S.A. Dange edited The Socialist; M.N. Roy edited Vanguard and Muzaffar Ahmad edited Navayug and Langal.

s: Which was the first communist paper of India?
x: M.N. Roy's Vanguard was the first communist paper; Kranti was a CPI Marathi weekly.

s: 'Kranti' was a weekly of the Communist Party in which language?
x: Kranti was the CPI's Marathi weekly.

s: Who led the Forward Bloc branch in Andhra?
x: Madduri Annapurnayya led the Forward Bloc Andhra branch.

s: Where was the Andhra unit of the Congress Socialist Party founded in 1934?
x: It was founded at Vijayawada on 23 June 1934; Guntur hosted its first conference in 1935.

s: Under whose leadership was the first conference of the Andhra Congress Socialist Party held at Guntur in 1935?
x: The first conference of the Andhra Congress Socialist Party was held at Guntur in 1935 under Tenneti Viswanatham.

s: Who was the first President of the Andhra Socialist Party (Andhra unit of the Congress Socialist Party, 1934)?
x: Per the notes (APPSC 2019 key), N.G. Ranga was the first President of the Andhra Socialist Party (founded 23 June 1934, Vijayawada), with Madduri Annapurnaiah as secretary; some accounts name Annapurnaiah President. Tenneti Viswanatham presided over the first session at Guntur (1935).

s: Where was the Andhra Socialist Party founded on 23 June 1934?
x: The Andhra unit of the CSP was founded at Vijayawada; the all-India CSP was founded at Patna.

s: Who presided over the first session of the Andhra Socialist Party in 1935?
x: Tenneti Viswanatham presided over the first session in 1935.

s: Madduri Annapurnaiah was the first Secretary of which party formed in 1934?
x: The Andhra Socialist Party (Andhra unit of the CSP) was formed in 1934 with N.G. Ranga as President and Madduri Annapurnaiah as Secretary.

s: N.G. Ranga was the first President of which of the following bodies formed at Vijayawada in 1934?
x: The Andhra Socialist Party was founded at Vijayawada on 23 June 1934 with N.G. Ranga as its first President.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Socialist Party:
1. It was founded at Vijayawada in 1934.
2. Madduri Annapurnaiah was its first Secretary.
3. Its first session in 1935 was presided over by N.G. Ranga.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: It was founded at Vijayawada in 1934 with Annapurnaiah as Secretary, but its 1935 session was presided over by Tenneti Viswanatham.

s: Which Andhra leader, who joined the Congress Socialist Party after being jailed in the Salt Satyagraha, was called 'Andhra Netaji'?
x: Madduri Annapurnaiah (b. 1899, Komaragiri) was called 'Andhra Netaji'; jailed in the Salt Satyagraha, he then joined the CSP. N.G. Ranga founded the Andhra Socialist Party; Tenneti Viswanatham presided over its 1935 session; Sundarayya was a communist leader.

s: Who was the first Andhra leader to join the Forward Bloc and led its Andhra branch?
x: Madduri Annapurnaiah was the first Andhra leader in the Forward Bloc and led its Andhra branch. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao led the Andhra Swaraj Party (1934); N.G. Ranga founded the Andhra Socialist Party; Tenneti Viswanatham later founded the Kisan Mazdoor Party (1951).

s: With whom is the Andhra Swaraj Party (1934) associated?
x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao formed the Andhra Swaraj Party in 1934.

s: Tenneti Viswanatham left the Indian National Congress in which year to found the Kisan Mazdoor Party?
x: Tenneti Viswanatham left the Congress in 1951 to found the Kisan Mazdoor Party.

s: The Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party merged nationally with which party in 1952 to form the Praja Socialist Party?
x: The Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party merged with the Socialist Party in 1952, resulting in the formation of the Praja Socialist Party.

s: Which leader left the Congress, joined the KMPP and then led the Praja Socialist Party in Andhra?
x: Tanguturi Prakasam joined the KMPP and then led the PSP in Andhra.

s: In which year did J.B. Kripalani form the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party?
x: The KMPP was formed in 1951; it merged with the Socialist Party in 1952 to form the PSP.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 1952 Madras Assembly election:
1. The United Front chose Tanguturi Prakasam as its leader.
2. Governor Sri Prakasa invited Prakasam to form the government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The United Front chose Prakasam, but Governor Sri Prakasa invited Rajaji instead.

s: In 1953, which place did the Praja Socialist Party want to be made the capital of Andhra State?
x: The Praja Socialist Party wanted Tirupati to be the capital of Andhra State in 1953. Kurnool became the capital instead.

s: Which place was chosen as the capital of Andhra State in 1953, though the Praja Socialist Party wanted Tirupati?
x: The PSP wanted Tirupati, but Kurnool was chosen as capital in 1953.

s: How many seats did the Congress win in the 1955 Andhra Assembly election?
x: In 1955 the Congress won 119 seats (KLP 22, CPI 15, PSP 13, Praja Party 5).

s: Who edited the Telugu journal 'Udayini'?
x: Udayini was edited by Kompella Janardhana Rao, not Ranga, who edited Navayuga and Prajamitra.

s: Which was the first wholly socialist Telugu journal, started at Rajahmundry in 1937?
x: Navasakti, started at Rajahmundry on 15 December 1937, was the first wholly socialist Telugu journal.

s: Which publication was founded and edited by Madduri Annapurnaiah?
x: Madduri Annapurnaiah founded and edited the Congress newspaper.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Navya Sahitya Mala — Vidwan Viswam and Tarimela Nagi Reddy
x: Udayini was edited by Kompella Janardhana Rao, not N.G. Ranga. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which of the following were Telugu journals of N.G. Ranga?
x: Navayuga and Prajamitra were edited by N.G. Ranga.

s: In which year did N.G. Ranga set up the Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu?
x: Ranga set up the Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu in 1939.

s: Which of the following pairs of parties founded by N.G. Ranga and their years is correctly matched?
x: Ranga founded the Krishikar Lok Party in 1951. He founded the Andhra Socialist Party in 1934 and the Swatantra Party in 1959, not 1949.

s: Who founded the Raithu Rakshana Sangham (1934)?
x: N.G. Ranga founded the Raithu Rakshana Sangham in 1934, the year he also formed the Andhra Socialist Party.

s: In which year did N.G. Ranga help found the Swatantra Party?
x: Ranga founded the Krishikar Lok Party in 1951 and the Swatantra Party in 1959.

s: Whom was the Kooli Rakshana Samiti, formed at Guntur in March 1935, mainly meant to organise?
x: Because the CPI was banned, leftists organised workers and farm labourers through the Kooli Rakshana Samiti, formed at Guntur in March 1935.

s: Where and when were the Andhra Rashtra Yuva Mahasabhas held?
x: The Andhra Rashtra Yuva Mahasabha was held at Vizag in 1935 and at Kakinada in 1936. Annapurnaiah was prominent in these youth activities.

s: P. Sundarayya was the joint secretary of which youth meeting in 1935?
x: Sundarayya was joint secretary of the Vizag Yuva Mahasabha of 1935; the Kakinada Mahasabha was in 1936.

s: Under whose leadership was the Peasant Institute at Nidubrolu established during 1933–34?
x: N.G. Ranga organised the Peasant Institute at Nidubrolu in Guntur during 1933–34. It was India’s first peasant training institute.

s: Where was the first political summer school held in the summer of 1937?
x: Kothapatnam in Guntur district hosted the first political summer school in 1937.

s: Who organised the 1938 political school at Hindupur?
x: The Hindupur school of 1938 was run by the communist Idukallu Sadasivan; Ranga ran Madanapalle that year.

s: In which year was a socialist political school held at Madanapalle in Andhra?
x: Madanapalle is associated with 1938; Kothapatnam was 1937 and the Kankipadu Rajakeeya Pathashala 1939.

s: Why did Andhra communists initially join Ranga’s Andhra Socialist Party?
o: To establish the Forward Bloc in Andhra
To contest elections independently of the Congress
Because the CPI was banned and they were advised to work inside the Congress
To support the Quit India Movement
x: After the CPI was banned, Andhra communists joined Ranga’s Andhra Socialist Party on Professor Gout’s advice so that they could work inside the Congress.

s: Which development widened the break between socialists and communists during the Second World War?
o: The CPI was unbanned on 23 July 1934.
The communists supported Quit India and opposed the People’s War.
The socialists dissolved the Andhra Socialist Party in 1936.
The communists supported the People’s War in 1941 and opposed Quit India.
x: The communists’ support for the People’s War in 1941 and opposition to the Quit India Movement widened the political break with the socialists.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Communist Party:
1. It was formally founded at Kakinada in January 1936.
2. Chandra Rajeswara Rao was its secretary at the founding.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: P. Sundarayya was its secretary when it was formally founded at Kakinada in January 1936. Hence 1 only.

s: In which year did the Congress Socialist Party expel the communists?
x: The CSP expelled the communists in 1940; the 'People's War' line of 1941 widened the break.

s: In which year was the Andhra Communist Party formed at Kakinada?
x: The Andhra Communist Party was formed at Kakinada in January 1936 with P. Sundarayya as Secretary.

s:
Consider the following statements about the first observance of Labour Day in India:
1. It was observed in 1923 at Madras.
2. It was organised by the Forward Bloc.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it was organised by Singaravelu's Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan (the Forward Bloc came much later). Hence 1 only.

s: Who presided over the 1935 Siricilla session of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha?
x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao presided at Siricilla in 1935. Ravi Narayana Reddy presided at Chilkur (1941) and Bhuvanagiri (1944), and K.V. Ranga Reddy at Hyderabad (1943).

s: Who presided over the first session of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha, held at Jogipet in 1930?
x: The official key (G2 2011) gives Suravaram Pratap Reddy as president of the first session at Jogipet (Medak), 1930. One book names Madapati Hanumantha Rao, who presided at Siricilla in 1935 - a trap. Ravi Narayana Reddy presided in 1941, 1944 and 1945; K.V. Ranga Reddy in 1943.

s: Who presided over the 1943 Hyderabad session of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha, the first contested presidency?
x: K.V. Ranga Reddy presided over the 1943 Hyderabad session, the first contested presidency.

s: Who presided over the 1941 Chilkur session of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha?
x: Ravi Narayana Reddy presided over the Chilkur (1941), Bhuvanagiri (1944) and Khammam (1945) sessions.

s: The Vandemataram Struggle of 1938 was associated with which university?
x: The 1938 Vandemataram Struggle took place at Osmania University, when students sang Vandemataram against the Nizam's ban.

s: With which organisation was Makhdoom Mohiuddin associated?
x: Makhdoom Mohiuddin was associated with the Hyderabad State Comrades Association, established in 1939.

s: In which year was the Hyderabad State Comrades Association, the first communist unit in Telangana, formed?
x: The Hyderabad State Comrades Association, regarded as Telangana's first communist unit, was formed in 1939. Its members included Makhdoom Mohiuddin, Raj Bahadur Gour and Syed Ibrahim.

s: Who presided over the inaugural meeting of the Hyderabad State Comrades Association (1939)?
x: Kashinath Rao Vaidya presided over the inaugural meeting of the Comrades Association, Telangana's first communist unit.

s: Who among the following was a member of the Hyderabad State Comrades Association?
x: Makhdoom Mohiuddin, Raj Bahadur Gour and Syed Ibrahim were members of the Comrades Association (1939).

s:
Consider the following statements about the 1944 Bhuvanagiri session of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha:
1. It brought the Mahasabha under communist control.
2. After it, a rival Nationalist Andhra Mahasabha broke away.
3. It was held at Siricilla.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: At Bhuvanagiri (1944) the Mahasabha came under communist control and a rival Nationalist Andhra Mahasabha broke away. Statement 3 is wrong: the session was at Bhuvanagiri, not Siricilla.

s: The Andhra Communist Party was formed at Kakinada in January 1936 with whom as Secretary?
x: P. Sundarayya was the Secretary of the Andhra Communist Party formed at Kakinada in January 1936.

s: Where was the second Communist Conference in Andhra, attended by P.C. Joshi, held in 1938?
x: The second Communist Conference was held at Vijayawada in 1938; the party itself was formed at Kakinada in 1936.

s: From which issue to which issue did communist activity shift the main focus of Andhra politics?
x: Through peasant mobilisation, the communists shifted Andhra politics from language to land.

s: Where was the Andhra Communist Party set up in January 1936?
x: The Andhra Communist Party was set up at Kakinada in January 1936. Vijayawada hosted the second (1938) and third (1943) communist conferences.

s: At the 1934 secret communist meeting in Katragadda Narayana Rao's garden, Vijayawada, who became secretary?
x: The 1934 Vijayawada meeting formed a 7-member committee with P. Sundarayya as secretary.

s: Where was the 3rd conference of the Andhra communists (July 1943), the first open conference, held?
x: The 3rd conference, the first open one, met at Vijayawada in July 1943; Kakinada was the 1936 founding place.

s: Where was the Visalandhra Maha Sabha of July 1956, which merged the Andhra and Telangana communist units, held?
x: The Visalandhra Maha Sabha met at Hyderabad in July 1956 and merged the Andhra and Telangana communist units.

s: What was decided at the Visalandhra Maha Sabha held at Hyderabad in July 1956?
o: The Andhra and Telangana communist units were merged
The Communist Party split into CPI and CPI(M)
The Telangana armed struggle was called off
The Andhra Communist Party was founded
x: At the July 1956 Visalandhra Maha Sabha in Hyderabad, the Andhra and Telangana communist units merged.

s: On which date was the ban on the Communist Party of India lifted?
x: The ban on the Communist Party of India was lifted on 23 July 1942.

s: In which year was the ban on the Communist Party in Andhra (Madras), imposed in 1949, lifted?
x: The Andhra (Madras) ban ran from 1949 to 1951.

s: In which year was the Communist Party banned in Hyderabad State?
x: Hyderabad State banned the Communist Party in December 1946. The all-India ban ran from 1934 to 1942, and Andhra (Madras) banned it in 1949.

s: In which year was the Communist Party of India banned, a ban that also covered the Madras Presidency?
x: The CPI was banned on 23 July 1934; the ban was lifted on 23 July 1942.

s: For how many years did the ban on the Communist Party of India, imposed on 23 July 1934, last?
x: The ban was imposed on 23 July 1934 and lifted on 23 July 1942 - exactly eight years later.

s: In which year was the communist paper Prajasakti banned?
x: Prajasakti was banned in 1948; Prakasam had arrested communist leaders in 1946.

s: P. Sundarayya was the first person to hold which of the following posts in Andhra Pradesh?
o: President of the Andhra Congress Committee
x: P. Sundarayya was the first Leader of the Opposition in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Telangana People's Struggle and its Lessons – K. Lingaraju
x: Telangana People's Struggle and its Lessons is by P. Sundarayya, not K. Lingaraju, who rendered Gorky's Mother into Telugu.

s: Which journal was the organ of the Communist Party in Andhra?
x: Prajasakti was the Andhra CPI organ.

s: Who started the newspaper 'Visalandhra'?
x: The newspaper Visalandhra was started by P. Sundarayya.

s: P. Sundarayya hailed from Alaganipadu in which district?
x: P. Sundarayya (Sundara Ramireddy) was from Alaganipadu, Nellore.

s: Which pair of leaders went with the CPI(M) after the 1964 split in the communist movement?
o: Ravi Narayana Reddy and Chandra Rajeswara Rao
P. Sundarayya and Ravi Narayana Reddy
x: P. Sundarayya and Basavapunnaiah went with the pro-China CPI(M), while Ravi Narayana Reddy and Chandra Rajeswara Rao remained with the pro-Soviet CPI.

s: Which communist leader won the Nalgonda seat in 1952 with the highest majority in India?
x: Ravi Narayana Reddy (CPI) won Nalgonda in 1952 with India's highest majority and stayed with the CPI in 1964. Sundarayya became AP's first Leader of the Opposition and joined the CPI(M); Baddam Yella Reddy organised agrarian struggles; Makhdoom Mohiuddin was a poet and Comrades Association leader.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: P. Sundarayya — CPI and later CPI(M)
x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha was a leader of the Hyderabad State Congress and led the Join Indian Union movement; he was not a CPI(M) leader. Ravi Narayana Reddy, Baddam Yella Reddy and P. Sundarayya were associated with the communist movement.

s: Who was Andhra Pradesh's first Leader of the Opposition?
x: P. Sundarayya, who joined the CPI(M) in 1964, was AP's first Leader of the Opposition.

s: Who led the 'Join Indian Union' movement in Hyderabad State?
x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha of the Hyderabad State Congress led the 'Join Indian Union' movement.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 1964 split in the communist movement:
1. The CPI was pro-Soviet.
2. The CPI(M) was pro-China.
3. Ravi Narayana Reddy joined the CPI(M).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: In 1964 the CPI was pro-Soviet and the CPI(M) pro-China; Ravi Narayana Reddy stayed with the CPI.

s: Who wrote the work *Visalandhralo Prajarajyam* in 1946?
x: P. Sundarayya wrote *Visalandhralo Prajarajyam* in 1946.

s: Who edited Navasakti, the first Telugu communist paper?
x: Navasakti, the first Telugu communist paper, was published from Rajahmundry on 15 December 1937 with Chandra Rajeswara Rao as editor.

s: Who was the editor of Prajasakti, which began as a weekly in 1942 and became a daily in 1945?
x: Prajasakti was edited by Maddukuri Chandrasekhara Rao. Chandra Rajeswara Rao edited Navasakti from Rajahmundry (1937).

s: Who inaugurated the Visalandhra daily, started at Vijayawada on 22 June 1952?
x: Tapi Dharma Rao inaugurated Visalandhra, which replaced the banned Prajasakti.

s: Which memoir was written by Ravi Narayana Reddy?
x: Ravi Narayana Reddy wrote Veera Telangana – Naa Anubhavalu, Gnapakalu. Visalandhralo Prajarajyam is by P. Sundarayya.

s: From which place was Navasakti, the first Telugu communist paper, published in 1937?
x: Navasakti, edited by Chandra Rajeswara Rao, came out from Rajahmundry on 15 December 1937.

s: Which daily was started at Vijayawada in 1952 in place of Prajasakti?
x: Visalandhra began on 22 June 1952 at Vijayawada in place of the banned Prajasakti.

s: Praja Natya Mandali, formed in 1943, was the Andhra wing of which organisation?
x: Praja Natya Mandali (1943) was the Andhra wing of IPTA, the CPI's cultural front.

s: Which folk form did Praja Natya Mandali use above all to carry political messages to villages?
x: Praja Natya Mandali relied above all on Burrakatha, especially during the Telangana struggle.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Praja Natya Mandali?
o: It was the cultural front of the CPI through IPTA
Garikapati Raja Rao was a leading organiser
It was founded by Gaddar in 1972
x: Gaddar's 1972 body was Jana Natya Mandali of the People's War Group; Praja Natya Mandali dates from 1943.

s: Who condemned the Madras Government's ban on the Kothapatnam summer school in a press statement on 17 June 1937?
x: Nehru condemned the ban on the Kothapatnam school in a press statement on 17 June 1937.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Kothapatnam summer school:
1. It was held in 1937.
2. It taught politics and economics to young activists.
3. The Madras Government supported it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 1937 Kothapatnam school taught politics and economics; the Madras Government banned it and police lathi-charged the students.

s: Who led the Kalukova satyagraha at Munagala (1938)?
x: The Munagala (Kalukova) struggle was led by Nanduri Prasada Rao, backed by Chandra Rajeswara Rao. Peta Chapanayya was jailed in the Challapalli struggle of 1942.

s: The Challapalli peasant struggle of 1942 was associated with which pair of communist leaders?
o: Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya
Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao
x: The Challapalli struggle in Krishna district in 1942 was led by Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya, who was jailed.

s: Who led the Kalipatnam peasant struggle (1938-39) in West Godavari?
x: Sundarayya and Kommareddy led Kalipatnam; Nanduri Prasada Rao led Munagala and Chandra Rajeswara Rao Challapalli.

s: During which period did the Srikakulam Girijana struggle take place?
x: The Srikakulam Girijana struggle is dated 1968-1970 (G2 2017 key); it was crushed by 1971. 1946-51 is the Telangana Armed Struggle, 1922-24 Alluri's Rampa rebellion and 1938-44 Komaram Bheem's Gond movement.

s: Doddi Komaraiah was killed at which place on 4 July 1946, triggering the Telangana Armed Struggle?
x: Doddi Komaraiah was killed by the deshmukh's men at Kadavendi in Jangaon on 4 July 1946, triggering the Telangana Armed Struggle.

s: Where were Vempatapu Satyam and Adibhatla Kailasam of the Srikakulam struggle killed on 10 July 1970?
x: Satyam and Kailasam were killed at Barikonda on 10 July 1970. Jalantra Kota is where Panchadhi Krishnamurthy was killed on 27 May 1969.

s: Who founded the People's War Group in 1980?
x: Kondapalli Seetharamaiah founded the People's War Group in 1980. The other three were leaders of the Srikakulam Girijan struggle.

s: When did the Telangana Armed Struggle end with a ceasefire?
x: The struggle (1946-1951) ended with a ceasefire in October 1951 after Soviet advice.

s: Near which place was the tribal meeting attacked on 31 October 1967, which triggered the Srikakulam struggle?
x: The trigger was the attack near Parvathipuram (Mondemkhal incident); Barikonda is where the leaders were killed in 1970.

s:
Consider the following statements about the armed struggles:
1. The Telangana Armed Struggle lasted from 1946 to 1951.
2. The Srikakulam struggle lasted from 1968 to 1970.
3. The Telangana struggle was triggered by the killing of Doddi Komaraiah at Kadavendi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: Telangana 1946-1951 (triggered by Doddi Komaraiah's killing at Kadavendi, 4 July 1946) and Srikakulam 1968-1970.

s: Whose killing at Kadavendi in Jangaon on 4 July 1946 triggered the Telangana Armed Struggle?
x: Doddi Komaraiah was killed by a deshmukh's men at Kadavendi on 4 July 1946, which set off the Telangana Armed Struggle. The others were Srikakulam leaders.

s: Where was Panchadhi Krishnamurthy of the Srikakulam struggle killed in May 1969?
x: Panchadhi Krishnamurthy was killed at Jalantra Kota on 27 May 1969.

s: During the Telangana Armed Struggle, what did the peasants set up in the villages after seizing land?
x: In the Telangana struggle peasants seized land and set up village soviets.

s: Komaram Bheem led the movement (1938-44) of which tribe?
x: Komaram Bheem led the Gond movement of 1938-44.

s: The Vishalandhra movement was started by the:
x: The Vishalandhra movement was started by the Communist Party (APPSC 2012), not the Congress Socialist Party.

s: In the 1952 elections, how many of the 145 Andhra-region seats did the communists win?
x: The communists won 41 of 145 Andhra-region seats in 1952.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the communist position on Visalandhra is correct?
o: The communists were the first to demand Visalandhra in 1946 and initiated the movement.
The communists opposed the formation of linguistic states from the beginning.
The demand for Visalandhra was first raised only after 1955.
The communists supported Visalandhra but did not participate in its movement.
x: The communists were the first to demand Visalandhra in 1946 and started the movement. They did not oppose linguistic states.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: CPI's 'People's War' line – decisive CPI win in the 1945–46 elections
CPI's opposition to Quit India – immediate CPI split in 1964
CPI's 'People's War' line – loss in the 1945–46 elections
CPI's opposition to Quit India – formation of Praja Natya Mandali
x: The 'People's War' line and opposition to the Quit India Movement cost the CPI the 1945–46 elections.

s: On which date did Prakasam's first Andhra State ministry fall after a communist-led agitation?
x: Prakasam's ministry fell on 15 November 1954; the CPI then won only 15 of 196 seats in 1955.

s: Who were the first to demand Visalandhra, in 1946?
x: The communists first demanded Visalandhra in 1946 and started the movement (G2 2012).

s: How many of the 196 seats did the CPI win in the 1955 Andhra State elections?
x: After Prakasam's ministry fell in 1954, the CPI won only 15 of 196 seats in 1955.

s:
Arrange in chronological order:
A. Gandhi's fast unto death begins
B. Poona Pact
C. Communal Award announced
x: Communal Award (16 Aug 1932), Gandhi's fast (20 Sept 1932), Poona Pact (24 Sept 1932).

s: Where did Gandhi begin his fast unto death against the Communal Award on 20 September 1932?
x: Gandhi began his fast unto death in Yerwada Jail, Poona, on 20 September 1932, arguing that separate electorates for Dalits would permanently divide Hindu society.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ambedkar-Gandhi debate of 1932:
1. Gandhi held that separate electorates for Dalits would permanently divide Hindu society.
2. Ambedkar supported the separate electorate given by the Communal Award.
3. Ambedkar refused to sign the Poona Pact.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Gandhi opposed and Ambedkar supported the separate electorate; Ambedkar signed the Poona Pact, accepting a joint electorate.

s: On which date did Gandhi begin his fast unto death against the Communal Award?
x: The fast began on 20 September 1932 at Yerwada; 16 Aug was the Award and 24 Sept the Poona Pact.

s: The reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes under the constitutional system is conceptually linked to which feature of the Poona Pact?
o: Nomination by the British Prime Minister
x: The Poona Pact's model of joint electorates with reserved seats became the basis for the constitutional approach to SC political reservation.

s: Who signed the Poona Pact on behalf of the caste Hindus?
x: Malaviya signed for the caste Hindus and Ambedkar for the depressed classes.

s: How many provincial seats were reserved for the Depressed Classes under the Poona Pact?
x: The Pact reserved 148 seats, against 71 under the Award.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Poona Pact?
o: It kept the separate electorate for the Depressed Classes
B.R. Ambedkar signed it for the Depressed Classes
It provided reserved seats in a joint electorate
x: The Pact dropped the separate electorate and gave reserved seats in a joint electorate.

s: Who signed the Rajah-Moonje Pact of February 1932 on reserved seats in joint electorates with M.C. Rajah?
x: M.C. Rajah and B.S. Moonje of the Hindu Mahasabha made the pact; Ambedkar opposed it.

s: Who founded the Depressed Classes Mission on 18 October 1906?
x: Vitthal Ramji Shinde founded the Depressed Classes Mission in 1906.

s: Which body, founded in 1924, had the motto 'Educate, Agitate, Organise'?
x: Ambedkar founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha on 20 July 1924 with this motto.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Jagan Mitra Mandali – Bhagya Reddy Varma
x: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was Gandhi's body with G.D. Birla as president; M.C. Rajah led the All India Depressed Classes Association.

s: Who was the first president of the All India Anti-Untouchability League, founded by Gandhi in 1932?
x: Gandhi founded the League on 30 September 1932, but its first president was G.D. Birla; Amritlal Thakkar was its secretary.

s: Who was the first secretary of the All India Anti-Untouchability League founded by Gandhi in 1932?
x: G.D. Birla was its first president and Amritlal Thakkar its secretary.

s: By what name did the All India Anti-Untouchability League (1932) later come to be known?
x: The League was renamed the Harijan Sevak Sangh; they are the same body.

s: Who founded the Adi Hindu Social Service League?
x: The Adi Hindu Social Service League grew out of Bhagya Reddy Varma's work in Hyderabad.

s: Who founded the Independent Labour Party in August 1936?
x: Ambedkar founded the ILP in 1936; it won 15 of 17 seats contested in 1937.

s: Who was the president of the All India Depressed Classes Association?
x: M.C. Rajah headed the All India Depressed Classes Association (Nagpur).

s: In which year did Ambedkar form the All India Scheduled Castes Federation?
x: Ambedkar formed the Federation in July 1942 with N. Sivaraj; 1936 was the ILP.

s: How many of the 17 seats it contested did Ambedkar's Independent Labour Party win in 1937?
x: The Independent Labour Party (1936) won 15 of the 17 seats it contested in 1937.

s: At the 1917 Vijayawada conference, by what name did Bhagya Reddy Varma argue the depressed classes should be called?
x: He held they were the original inhabitants, to be called Adi-Hindu, not Panchama.

s: From which body did Bhagya Reddy Varma receive the title 'Varma'?
x: The Arya Samaj gave him the title 'Varma'.

s: Who worked with Bhagya Reddy Varma to organise the Adi-Andhra movement among the Malas?
x: Arige Ramaswamy worked with Varma to organise the Adi-Andhra movement.

s: Which name was adopted by the 1917 Vijayawada conference of the depressed classes led by Bhagya Reddy Varma?
x: The 1917 Vijayawada conference rejected 'Panchama' and adopted the name Adi-Andhra Mahajana Sabha.

s: Whose first paper was Mooknayak ('leader of the voiceless'), started on 31 January 1920?
x: Mooknayak (1920) was Ambedkar's first paper.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Bahishkrit Bharat (1927) and Mooknayak (1920) were Ambedkar's; Harijan (1933) was Gandhi's.

s: Which of the following first used the term 'Scheduled Castes'?
x: The term was first used by the Simon Commission, fixed by the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first list was issued in 1936.

s: By which of the following was the term 'Scheduled Castes' fixed?
x: The Simon Commission first used the term in 1930; the GoI Act 1935 fixed it.

s: In which year was the first list of Scheduled Castes issued?
x: The first SC list came in 1936, after the term was fixed by the 1935 Act.

s: The Communal Award of 1932 followed the failure of which conference over minority representation?
x: The 2nd Round Table Conference failed over minority representation, leading to the Communal Award.

s: For purposes of representation, the Communal Award of 1932 divided Indians into how many groups?
x: The Communal Award divided Indians into 11 groups and recognised the Depressed Classes as a minority.

s: Under the Communal Award, what share of seats in all provinces except the North-West Frontier Province was reserved for women?
x: The Communal Award reserved three per cent of seats for women in all provinces except the NWFP.

s: What did the Depressed Classes get under the Communal Award?
o: A double vote – one in a separate electorate and one in the general electorate
A single vote in the general electorate only
Two votes, both restricted to the separate electorate
No vote, but nomination to provincial legislatures
x: The Depressed Classes received a double vote: one in a separate electorate and another in the general electorate.

s: How many seats in the provincial legislatures were the Depressed Classes to get under the Communal Award?
x: The Award gave the Depressed Classes 71 seats; the Poona Pact raised this to 148.

s: Which British Prime Minister announced the Communal Award in August 1932?
x: The Communal Award was announced on 16 August 1932 by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald, not by the Viceroy.

s: Which of the following was declared a minority and given a separate electorate for the first time by the Communal Award?
x: The Communal Award of 1932 declared the Depressed Classes a minority and gave them a separate electorate for the first time; Muslims had one since 1909.

s: On which date was the August Declaration on India's constitutional development made?
x: The August Declaration was made on 20 August 1917.

s: Which body exerted the chief political pressure that prompted the Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1917?
x: The Home Rule Leagues created political pressure that contributed to the British declaration recognising self-government as an objective.

s: What did the Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1917 announce as British policy?
o: immediate grant of dominion status to India
progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the British Empire
complete independence of India within ten years
provincial autonomy with an All-India Federation
x: On 20 August 1917 Montagu announced the gradual development of self-governing institutions with a view to the progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the Empire - the first official recognition of self-government as an aim. Dominion status as a goal came with the 1929 Deepavali Declaration; complete independence was never promised then; provincial autonomy and federation came with the 1935 Act.

s: Who led the Moderates who accepted the 1919 reforms, left the Congress and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation?
x: Surendranath Banerjee and other Moderates accepted the reforms and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.

s: How did the Amritsar Congress of 1919 describe the reforms?
x: The Amritsar Congress characterised the reforms as inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing.

s: What did the 27-member Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao demand when it met Montagu at Madras?
o: A separate Muslim province in South India
Abolition of the Madras Legislative Council
x: The Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao sought the creation of a separate Andhra province.

s: Besides Edwin Montagu, after whom is the dyarchy scheme of the Government of India Act, 1919 named?
x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms are named after Secretary of State Edwin Montagu and Viceroy Lord Chelmsford.

s: Which post did Edwin Montagu, after whom the 1919 reforms are partly named, then hold?
x: Montagu was Secretary of State for India; Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy.

s: Who presided over the special Bombay session of the Congress (August 1918) that condemned the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms?
x: The special Bombay session of August 1918, presided by Hasan Imam, condemned the reforms.

s:
Match the following reactions to the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms:
List-I
A. C.R. Das and Tilak
B. Gandhi and Malaviya
C. Surendranath Banerjee
List-II
1. Give the reforms a fair trial
2. Rejected the reforms
3. Accepted the reforms and formed the Liberal Federation
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: C.R. Das and Tilak rejected the reforms, Gandhi and Malaviya wanted a fair trial, and Surendranath Banerjee's Moderates accepted them.

s: Which paper described the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms as 'giving with the right hand, taking with the left'?
x: Krishna Patrika described the reforms as 'giving with the right hand, taking with the left'.

s: Who presided over the Special Andhra Mahasabha held at Guntur on 17 August 1918?
x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao presided over the Special Andhra Mahasabha at Guntur in August 1918.

s: In which year was the Montagu-Chelmsford Report announced?
x: Montagu and Chelmsford toured India from December 1917; their Report was announced in July 1918.

s: Which was the upper chamber of the bicameral central legislature under the Government of India Act, 1919?
x: The 1919 Act created a bicameral central legislature with the Council of State as the upper chamber and the Legislative Assembly as the lower chamber.

s: On what basis did the Government of India Act, 1919 introduce direct elections?
o: Separate nomination by the Secretary of State
x: The Act introduced direct elections, but the franchise remained limited by property, tax and educational qualifications.

s: Apart from the Commander-in-Chief, how many members did the Viceroy's Executive Council have under the Government of India Act, 1919?
x: Apart from the Commander-in-Chief, the Council had six members, three of whom were Indians.

s: How many of the 145 members of the Legislative Assembly under the 1919 Act were elected?
x: The Assembly had 145 members, 104 elected; the Council of State had 60.

s: How many members did the Council of State, the upper house under the Government of India Act, 1919, have?
x: The Council of State had 60 members; the Legislative Assembly had 145 (104 elected).

s: After how many years did the statutory review provision of the Government of India Act, 1919 require the appointment of a commission?
x: The Act required a statutory commission to review its working after ten years. The Simon Commission was appointed two years early under this provision.

s: In which year was the Public Service Commission, provided for under Section 96(C) of the 1919 Act, set up?
x: The Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926, after the Lee Commission, not in 1921 when the Act came into force.

s: In which year was the Chamber of Princes (Narendra Mandal) set up by royal proclamation?
x: The Chamber of Princes, a consultative body of Indian rulers, was set up in 1921 under the 1919 reforms, not under the 1935 Act.

s: The Muddiman Committee (1924) was the British response to whose demand for a review of the 1919 Act?
x: The Muddiman Committee (1924) was the British response to the Swarajist demand for a review of the Government of India Act, 1919.

s: Who was the first High Commissioner for India in London, an office provided by the 1919 Act?
x: Sir William Meyer became the first High Commissioner in 1920.

s: On whose recommendations was the Public Service Commission of 1926 set up?
x: The PSC came on 1 October 1926 after the Lee Commission.

s: The Public Service Commission in India was provided for by Section 96(C) of which Act?
x: Section 96(C) of the Government of India Act, 1919 provided for a Public Service Commission, which was set up in 1926.

s: Which Act first introduced direct elections in India?
x: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections. The 1909 Act introduced elected non-official members mainly through indirect and separate electorates.

s: Dyarchy was criticised because ministers held transferred subjects; what kind of subject was finance?
x: Ministers controlled transferred subjects, but finance remained a reserved subject, so they lacked financial control.

s: Into which categories did dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919 divide provincial subjects?
x: Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces and divided provincial subjects into reserved and transferred subjects.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about provincial dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: Provincial subjects were divided into reserved and transferred subjects.
Transferred subjects were administered by the Governor with ministers.
Local self-government was a reserved subject.
Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor with the Executive Council.
x: Local self-government was a transferred subject, administered by the Governor with ministers, not a reserved subject.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: Direct elections to the central legislature
Creation of the office of High Commissioner for India in London
Separation of provincial budgets from the central budget
Provincial autonomy in place of dyarchy
x: Provincial autonomy was associated with the Government of India Act, 1935. The 1919 Act introduced dyarchy in the provinces, along with the other listed features.

s: Under provincial dyarchy of 1919, which of the following was a transferred subject?
x: Local self-government, education and health were transferred; police, land revenue and justice were reserved.

s: At which level did the federation proposed under the Government of India Act, 1935 provide for dyarchy?
o: Both the Centre and the provinces
x: The 1935 Act provided dyarchy at the Centre, while replacing dyarchy in the provinces with provincial autonomy.

s: Which Act introduced dual control through the Board of Control and the Court of Directors?
x: Pitt's India Act (1784) set up dual control; the Regulating Act (1773) created the Governor-General of Bengal.

s: Which office was created by the Regulating Act of 1773?
x: The Regulating Act created the Governor-General of Bengal and a Supreme Court.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Government of India Act, 1919 – Morley-Minto Reforms
Pitt's India Act, 1784 – Board of Control
Government of India Act, 1935 – Provincial autonomy
x: The 1919 Act is the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms; Morley-Minto is the Indian Councils Act, 1909.

s: Which Act was popularly known as the Morley-Minto Reforms?
x: Morley-Minto Reforms = Indian Councils Act 1909; the 1919 Act = Montagu-Chelmsford.
